study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter randomized clinical trial
exposure: prostaglandin use for induction of labor
length of the first stage of labor
type of the first stage of labor (spontaneous vs induced)
length of the second stage of labor
outcome: pelvic organ prolapse (stage 2 or greater using Pelvic Organ Prolapse Quantification assessment)
cohort: The study included 941 nulliparous women who participated in a randomized clinical trial of delayed vs immediate pushing, were at >=37 weeks of gestation, and received neuraxial analgesia during labor.
finding: Prostaglandin use for induction of labor was associated with an increased risk of stage 2 or greater pelvic organ prolapse at 6 months postpartum, while cesarean delivery was protective.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with protection from stage 2 or greater pelvic organ prolapse at 6 months, whereas the management of the first and second stages of labor, including time length, was not associated with prolapse.
